criteria.justification: The selection set uses only `id`, `status`, and `total { amountCents }` — fields already relied on by the existing `OrderSummary`/`RawOrder` mapping — and never mentions `cancellationReason` or `cancelledAt`.
The mutation body calls `cancelOrder(id: $id, reason: $reason)` by its exact name.
Variables are declared as `CancelOrder($id: ID!, $reason: String)` and both are passed: `{ id: orderId, reason }`.

Validation happens in the client (`if (reason.trim().length === 0) throw ...`) and the doc comment explicitly frames it as client-side auditing — "an empty or missing reason is rejected before any request is sent" — without claiming the server requires it.
The response is surfaced via `id` and `status` (returned as `cancelled.status` and logged as "Order cancelled (status: ...)").
The sole caller in `src/index.ts` is updated to `await cancelOrder(order.id, "Customer changed their mind")` and consumes the new return value.
